Subject: Post-call recap + ask: latency / tokens A/B tests

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can set expectations for the comparative lab run you asked about:

What we heard
- Primary ask: apples-to-apples latency/throughput comparison vs the Hyperscaler API for your chat flow (multi-turn with 1-3 messages, average 350 tokens per conversation).
- Key metrics: p95 and p99 token latency, tokens/sec steady-state, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Constraints: no PHI in the test corpus. Procurement will need invoice/PO details and a short NDA for test keys.

Proposed Redwood plan
1) Canary: small A/B run (2k requests) to validate request shaping and KV cache warmup.
2) Full run: 100k request sweep across two variants (Redwood-hosted model vs Hyperscaler API variant) measuring p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and end-to-end tail latency under a steady 300 tokens/sec injection per instance for 2 hours.
3) Results: CSV with per-request latencies, summary p95/p99, token throughput, and cost extrapolation.

What we need from you
- A synthetic payload set (or permission to use the sample snippets you showed) — ideally 500 conversations covering typical turn counts.
- Any IP/PII rules for the dataset (you mentioned no PHI).
- Test account/keys or an allowlist for our test runner (short-lived preferred).
- Procurement contact to start the procurement paperwork and the NDA (Procurement cc'd?).

Tentative timeline
- Canary (internal): 48 hours after we get sample payloads
- Full run & analysis: 3 business days after canary completes

I'll hold off on running anything until we get the sample files and confirmation on test keys. Marcus will lead the lab execution and Neha will handle the inference config + quantization profile.

Thanks —
Jonas

Jonas / team —

Draft lab plan below. Attaching a stub CSV we'll populate after the canary (redwood-lab-results-iter1.csv).

Lab plan (high level)
- Canary (09/14): 2,000 requests, 3 ramp phases (0–60s ramp, 60–180s medium, 180–1200s steady). Use a single LLM variant (baseline) to validate shaping and KV cache warm.
- Full A/B sweep (09/15): 100k requests split 50/50 across Redwood endpoint vs Hyperscaler API wrapper.
  - Measurement windows: 15s sliding windows for tokens/sec, collect per-request latency, and compute p50/p95/p99 on aggregated request latency and on per-token latency (latency divided by token count).
  - Tokens/sec target: steady-state 300 tokens/sec per instance; run multiple parallel runners to reach the aggregate injection profile.
  - Repeat runs: 3 identical sweeps with different random seeds for request ordering to catch variance.
- Config notes:
  - Quantization: run float16 and int8-quant profiles where supported; ensure the Hyperscaler variant is configured to its closest equivalent if possible.
  - Cache warm: pre-warm prefix cache with first 5k requests identical to top-conversation shapes.

Deliverables
- redwood-lab-results-iter1.csv (per-request latencies + token counts)
- summary: p50/p95/p99 table, tokens/sec plot, cost projection per 1M tokens
- short write-up on any observed discrepancy (kernel/kv warm, tail variability).

I'll spin up the runners once Alex confirms keys/allowlist and we have the final payload. Using the HubSpot link Jonas included to tie the lab results back to the deal.

Cheers,
